source.publication: 2025 SC1040 Individual Income Tax Instructions (SCDOR) and the 2025 SC1040 form and tax tables (IITPacket_2025)
source.section: Instructions PDF p.12 'Line p-4 through line p-6: Military retirement deduction'; Instructions PDF pp.10-11 'Line p-1 through line p-3: Retirement deduction', qualified retirement income definition and Worksheet for taxpayer (line p-1) lines 1-5; Instructions PDF p.12 'Line q: Age 65 and older deduction' and Worksheet for taxpayer (line q-1) lines 1-4; PDF p.13 Examples 1-5 (Example 4); SC1040 lines 1-6 and 15 (packet PDF pp.46-47); Instructions PDF p.5 Line 1 (federal taxable income); Instructions PDF p.16 Line 6; Tax Rate Schedule packet PDF p.51 (6% minus 642, any filing status); brackets as derived in the record (brackets.derivation)

worked: Federal AGI = wages 30,000.00 + military pension 36,000.00 = 66,000.00. Federal taxable income = 66,000.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (15,750.00 single + 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older) = 48,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored, federal figures given, not tested). SC1040 line 1 federal taxable income 48,250.00; additions lines a-e none, line 2 = 0.00; line 3 = 48,250.00. Line p-4 military deduction 36,000.00 (uncapped, above 15,000, as Example 4). Line p-1 worksheet: 10,000.00 - 36,000.00 less than zero, 0.00. Line q-1 worksheet: 15,000.00 - (0.00 + 36,000.00) less than zero, 0.00 (no additional amount on q-1). Projection: military 36,000; both best_of_group caps reduced to 0. Line 4 total subtractions = p-4 36,000.00 = 36,000.00. Line 5 South Carolina income subject to tax = 48,250.00 - 36,000.00 = 12,250.00. Line 6 tax = 3% x (12,250.00 - 3,560.00) = 3% x 8,690.00 = 260.70; the printed table (row 12,200 to 12,300, figured at the row midpoint) gives 261; expected uses the bracket formula on the exact income. Line 12 Two Wage Earner Credit: not modelled (warning), 0.00; it is for joint filers only, so 0 anyway. Line 14 credits 0.00; line 15 state income tax = 260.70.
accepted_approximations: The bracket starts 3,560 and 17,840 are derived from the printed tax table and the 6%-minus-642 formula; the table fixes them only to 3,559-3,566 and 17,818-17,857. Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses the table row's midpoint.

The booklet stacks the age 65 deduction on the retirement deduction (15,000 less the retirement and military deductions taken). The projection puts the 65-or-older retirement deduction and the age 65 deduction in one best_of_group, with the age 65 cap reduced by military retirement. For a person 65 or older this gives the same total as the worksheets, the larger of 15,000 and the military retirement income (Examples 1-5), whenever the person's income covers it.
